cases.C23: Penstock makes the control architecture tangible: a recognised industrial flow regulator, sober and memorable, with clear domains and Companies House availability; its only concern is manageable sound-alike risk.
cases.C20: VeritasGate Labs makes governance explicit: truth plus controlled access, credible for regulated buyers and available across domains; its drawback is familiarity, while the full compound remains distinctive.
cases.C16: Imprimatur signals exactly what CISOs want: formal sign-off before action. The ecclesiastical root reads as gravitas, not gimmick; 'Labs' modernises it, and all key domains are free.
cases.C11: Cautia is short, ownable, and phonetically clean once heard ('caw-tee-a'), evoking caution without being a plain dictionary word. Cautio is a distinct spelling in a different niche (dashcams).
cases.C12: Directly captures human-in-the-loop control for CISOs; 'Labs' cleanly distinguishes it as a broader consultancy-to-product enterprise from single-feature runtime tools like veto.so, with clear UK registry and key domains.
cases.C14: Deliberately formal tone signals serious enterprise governance to regulated buyers; 'Labs' clearly separates it from biometric ID verification apps, securing full domain coverage including .com and clean UK registration.
cases.C29: Archaic, yes—but precision aids memory: a seneschal stewards power only under strict instruction. The word is ownable, domains clear, and the governance metaphor outweighs spelling friction.
cases.C31: Existing Vallum uses are adjacent, not 'Vallum Labs'; vallumlabs.ai/.co.uk are free. The Roman boundary metaphor precisely fits gated AI actions—sober, memorable, and distinct enough for UK company registration.
cases.C26: Chary (CHAIR-ee) names cautious least-privilege posture; charity misread fades once pronounced, and all key domains are free—sober, wry, registrable.
cases.C17: Seneschal (SEN-uh-shul) means delegated, revocable authority—the architecture in one word. Domain scarcity aside, the metaphor is precise, memorable, CISO-sober.
cases.C22: The offshore association actually reinforces the brand: Jersey and Guernsey bailiwicks are famed for strict data-protection regulation, precisely the CISO sensibility needed. The jurisdiction metaphor maps directly to bounded agent authority.
cases.C30: Provost literally means 'put in charge' — the sole officer who delegates bounded authority and demands accountability. That is exactly the architecture of distrust. University admin runs billion-pound regulated enterprises; the title signals governance rigour,
cases.C24: Claustra evokes precise gating—locks open only where authorized—aligning with the distrust architecture. Latin gravitas feels weighty yet modern; claustrophobia risk is mitigated by context and brand storytelling.
cases.C27: Anchorite signals disciplined confinement: agents operate only within sanctioned boundaries, mirroring trusted isolation. The historic nuance adds wit without implying antisocial behavior, differentiating from generic security terms.
cases.C15: It transforms revocation into a security asset. While 'countermanding' sounds disruptive, for a CISO, the absolute power to override autonomous AI is the primary requirement for regulated trust.
cases.C25: Runnymede Labs powerfully embodies constrained AI—power accepting limits, as at Magna Carta. Council/Trust associations are minor; the name's constitutional gravitas and ownable domains (.ai, .io, .co.uk) outweigh them. Memorable, sober, wry without silliness.
